note: Set B carries the same core Flexinol actuator and energy-load facts as A but without A's six duplicate claims repeated under the misspelled name "Flexnoll®", its misbound spring-force claim, and its two chart fragments that give "Ms °C" as a value; B also adds the supported trend that Ms temperature decreases with increasing nickel content. A's larger count adds mostly repetitions and label fragments rather than new correct content, and it also invents a 0 °C @ 50 at% chart point. Both sets bind chart-title quotes to numeric Ms values and both garble the "cool, martensite phase" quote as "during the cool force".
remarks: Both sets miss the fact that each bay carries two mirrored, independently acting assemblies and the role of the spring as the strain-force element running the assembly length. Chart-derived claims (50 C @ 50 at%, -100 C @ 53 at%, 100 C @ 49 at%, -100 C @ 51 at%) are read off a small scatter plot and are approximate; the -100 C @ 53 at% point looks doubtful since the lowest points sit near 51.5-52 at%, and A's 0 °C @ 50 at% point is likewise questionable. Both use the chart title as the quote for numeric values, which does not support the numbers. A consistently misspells Flexinol as "Flexnoll" (counted as misread labels) and repeats six facts verbatim under that name.
